title: Keigo Basics: 尊敬語 & 謙譲語
description: Special honorific/humble verbs, お〜になる, お〜する, お〜ください, plus 〜なさい.

questions.prompt: はじめまして。{田中|たなか}と（　）。
questions.explanation: **申す** is the humble (謙譲語) form of 言う. Use it for yourself: 〜と申します = 'I am called …'.
notes: 申される mixes the humble 申す with the respectful られる. It's a well-known keigo error.
言われます is passive ('I am told'), not a polite self-introduction.
おっしゃる is honorific (尊敬語). It raises the subject, so you can't use it about yourself.
questions.translation: Nice to meet you. My name is Tanaka.

questions.prompt: {先生|せんせい}は{何|なん}と（　）か。
questions.explanation: **おっしゃる** is the honorific form of 言う, used for what a superior says. Note the ます-form: おっしゃ**い**ます.
notes: 参る is humble 行く/来る, not 'say'.
拝見する is humble 見る ('I look at'), not 'say'.
申す is humble, for your own speech. Using it for a teacher lowers them.

questions.prompt: {先生|せんせい}、コーヒーを（　）か。
questions.explanation: **召し上がる** is the honorific form of 食べる/飲む, used when offering food or drink to a superior.
notes: いただく is humble 食べる/飲む, for yourself. Using it about the teacher lowers them.
参る is humble 行く/来る.
おる is humble いる.
questions.translation: Professor, would you like some coffee?

questions.prompt: {部長|ぶちょう}は{今|いま}、{会議室|かいぎしつ}に（　）。
questions.explanation: **いらっしゃる** is the honorific form of いる/行く/来る, used for the actions of a superior such as a department head.
notes: ござる is the polite form of ある (for things), not for people.
参る is humble 行く/来る, and it lowers the boss.
おる is humble いる. Use it for yourself or your in-group when talking to outsiders, not for your boss inside the company.
questions.translation: The department head is in the meeting room right now.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}の{午後|ごご}、そちらに（　）。
questions.explanation: **参る** is the humble form of 行く/来る. You lower your own action toward the listener.
notes: おいでになる is honorific too, which is wrong for your own action.
いらっしゃる is honorific, so you can't use it about yourself.
召し上がる means 'eat/drink' (honorific).
questions.translation: I'll come to your place tomorrow afternoon.

questions.prompt: {先生|せんせい}の{作品|さくひん}を（　）しました。
questions.explanation: **拝見する** is the humble form of 見る: 'I (humbly) looked at your work'.
notes: 見られる + しました isn't grammatical.
お見する isn't used. 見る has the special humble form 拝見する.
ご覧になる is honorific 見る, for someone else's looking. ご覧しました isn't a form.
questions.translation: I (humbly) looked at your work, Professor.

questions.prompt: {社長|しゃちょう}はもうお{帰|かえ}り（　）。
questions.explanation: **お + ます-stem + になる** is the regular honorific (尊敬語) pattern: お帰りになる = '(the president) went home'.
notes: お〜する is the humble pattern (お持ちします), for your own actions. You can't use it for the president.
お帰りください is a request ('please go home'), not a statement that he left.
お〜いたす is the extra-humble pattern, which is also wrong for a superior's action.
questions.translation: The president has already gone home.

questions.prompt: お{荷物|にもつ}、（　）しましょうか。
questions.explanation: **お + ます-stem + する** is the humble pattern for actions you do for someone: お持ちします = 'I'll carry it for you'.
notes: ご is used with Sino-Japanese (漢語) nouns (ご案内します). 持つ is a native verb and takes お.
持ってしましょうか is ungrammatical. Use お持ちしましょうか or 持ちましょうか.
The pattern uses the ます-stem (持ち), not the て-form.
questions.translation: Shall I carry your luggage for you?

questions.prompt: （{店員|てんいん}が{客|きゃく}に）{少々|しょうしょう}お{待|ま}ち（　）。
questions.explanation: **お + ます-stem + ください** is a respectful request: お待ちください = 'Please wait'. You'll hear it constantly in shops.
notes: お待ちいたします is humble ('I will wait'), the same problem as お待ちします.
お待ちになります is a statement ('you will wait'), not a request.
お待ちします is humble ('I will wait'). The clerk is asking the customer to wait, not saying they themselves will wait.
questions.translation: (Clerk to customer) Please wait a moment.

questions.prompt: ご{飯|はん}の{前|まえ}に{手|て}を{洗|あら}い（　）。
questions.explanation: **ます-stem + なさい** is a firm command, used by parents to children or teachers to students: 洗いなさい = 'Wash (your hands)!'.
notes: 洗いましょうか means 'shall I wash?'. It's an offer, not an instruction.
洗いたい ('I want to wash') expresses your own wish.
ください follows the て-form (洗ってください), not the ます-stem 洗い.

questions.prompt: {先生|せんせい}も{明日|あした}のパーティーに（　）か。
questions.explanation: Asking about a superior's action requires the honorific: **いらっしゃる** (= 行く/来る/いる).
notes: 伺う is humble 行く/聞く, for your own visits. You can't use it for the teacher's action.
参る is humble, so it would lower the teacher.
おる is humble いる, and it's also the wrong verb meaning.
questions.translation: Will you be coming to tomorrow's party too, Professor?
